changelog: Replace C8 to keep the clause-closure/cohesion check but explicitly allow isolating sentence-initial function words or discourse markers when the remainder is a cohesive, self-contained clause and the isolated opener does not itself assert a contradicting proposition — addresses the primary finding about safe opener cuts in very-short latency bins.
findings: The prompt demotes boundaries whose remainder would contradict the prefix, but it accomplishes this by promoting the immediately adjacent cut — producing one-word or head-fragment pieces (bare aux/copula, determiner-only, numeral-only, noun stripped of postmodifiers) that harm very-short latency bins.

The prompt reflexively avoids cutting near sentence-openers/function words, but for very short latency budgets isolating an initial function word or discourse marker can be beneficial when the remainder is cohesive and non-contradictory.

diagnosis.why: Replacing C8 made the model more willing to isolate sentence‑initial function words/discourse markers (it started cutting immediately after openers). That behaviour produced small gains for slightly longer remainders (≤10 bin) where the remainder stayed cohesive, but increased harmful fragmentation in the shortest latency bins (≤3/≤5/≤7) by introducing extra early cuts and splitting predicates/NPs (illustrated by the 'However, ‖ a nationwide…' and fragmented predicate examples), leaving the overall change near zero.
diagnosis.lesson: A later revision should respect that permitting isolation of sentence‑initial openers can help when the remainder is sufficiently long/cohesive (benefit in ≤10) but currently increases fragmentation in the very-short bins, so the change must not encourage immediate cuts after openers that produce very-short or predicate-splitting fragments.
